name: Assamese
notes: Standard (eastern) Assamese as described by Mahanta (2012) and Roy & Mahanta (2018), whose consonant tables agree segment for segment. Four properties separate it from Bengali and from Indo-Aryan generally, and the script it shares with Bengali hides all four. The Sanskrit sibilants ⟨শ ষ স⟩ merged to a velar fricative /x/, unique in Indo-Aryan. The retroflex series is written but not spoken: ⟨ট ঠ ড ঢ ণ⟩ have neutralised with the dentals to a single alveolar series /t tʰ d dʱ n/, so no /ʈ ɖ ɳ ɽ/ occurs. Affricates are absent as distinctive units, so ⟨চ ছ⟩ are /s/ and ⟨জ ঝ য⟩ are /z zʱ/ rather than the palatals their Bengali cognates spell. The one rhotic is the approximant /ɹ/, and ⟨ৰ⟩ and ⟨ৱ⟩ — the two letters in which the Assamese script differs from Bengali — write /ɹ/ and /w/. The eight-vowel system is /i e ɛ u ʊ o ɔ a/ with an ATR contrast; ⟨ও⟩ and ⟨ো⟩ write /ʊ/, not /o/, and ⟨এ⟩ and ⟨ে⟩ write /ɛ/. The inherent vowel is /ɔ/ and is not pronounced at the end of a word (inherent_vowel_final), except where deleting it would leave the word without a nucleus or manufacture a complex coda, which Assamese syllable structure does not permit. AS_X_BEFORE_CONSONANT states the cluster fronting xC → sC. The spirantisation of /kʰ/ to [x] is speaker- and register-dependent and is carried in the allophone table rather than as a reading of ⟨খ⟩. Two properties described in the sources are not encoded: regressive ATR vowel harmony raising /ɛ ɔ ʊ/ to /e o u/ before a high vowel, whose main target is the unwritten inherent vowel and so has no slot a rule can address; and the gemination of a consonant before ya-phala ⟨্য⟩.

sources.notes: Consonant table p.218 (twenty consonants: one alveolar plosive series, fricatives s z x h, approximant ɹ, no affricates, no retroflexes); vowel table p.220 (eight oral vowels i e ɛ u ʊ o ɔ ɑ); the retroflex/dental neutralisation and the /kʰ/ spirantisation are stated p.219, the ⟨ৰ⟩/⟨ৱ⟩ script difference in its footnote 2; vowel harmony p.221.

sources.author: Roy, S. & Mahanta, S.
sources.title: A Hybrid Approach to Grapheme to Phoneme Conversion in Assamese
sources.notes: Section 2 gives the akshara-to-phoneme rules: the inherent schwa is /ɔ/ and “is generally deleted in the end of a word”; “The consonant clusters xC becomes sC”; the vowel-harmony rules ε→e and ɔ→o before a following /i/ or /u/. Table 1 p.2830 repeats the consonant inventory, Table 2 p.2830 gives the vowels with ATR features. Section 4 notes Assamese admits no complex codas.

allophone_rules.notes: The velar fricative fronts to [s] in a cluster: Roy & Mahanta (2018) state the rule as “The consonant clusters xC becomes sC”, with /oboxtʰaːn/ → /obosthaːn/ ‘station’. Only a letter whose inherent vowel is suppressed by a hosonto reaches this slot bare, so the rule fires exactly in the cluster context it names.
